docs.what: Retitle 'US-05 — Self-healing loop and the operator stop'. Story: 'As an operator, I need the loop to keep delivering my intent — retrying, re-planning — and to wait for me rather than end on its own; only I stop it.' ACs: AC-05.1 Run states are exactly RUNNING, NEEDS_HUMAN, DONE, STOPPED; NEEDS_HUMAN carries a recovery reason and the resume command; NEEDS_HUMAN and STOPPED resume with /kpi <job>. AC-05.2 A review that repeats an output_fingerprint or failing AC set routes back to plan with repair.json (round, reason, failing_ac, evidence_ref, witness) as feedback. AC-05.3 Rounds are unbounded; the same witness repeating after its re-plan pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (no_progress) offering Give guidance / Keep going / Stop in the TUI and the resume command unattended. AC-05.4 Write outside write_allow pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (bounds) without a commit. AC-05.5 Untestable reviewer issue pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (review). AC-05.6 A transient 429 retry is not a new round; a provider refusal that cannot fail over pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (provider) with the real reason and the resume command. AC-05.7 Transient failures (http 408/429/5xx, timeout, transport) retry for as long as it takes with 1 s doubling backoff capped at 60 s, one node.retry event and one notification per retry, checkpoint before each wait. AC-05.8 No spend cap, clock, step, node-run or round counter ends a run; cost and elapsed time are reported only; a checkpoint written under a retired cap resumes. AC-05.9 /kpi stop writes STOPPED and stops a running loop at its next checkpoint; Ctrl+C mid-wait resumes into the same wait. AC-02.7: 'ROUND n'. AC-04.6: 'shows NEEDS_HUMAN (with its recovery) and did not execute'. AC-24.3: finished list becomes (DONE, NEEDS_HUMAN, STOPPED). AC-29.4 / AC-30.2: 'pauses implement NEEDS_HUMAN (research / stack)'. M-04 row: 'Bounds-violation fixture pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (bounds)'. Traceability table: US-05 -> RP-20.

risks: Removing every bound means an unattended job can run indefinitely (provider down for a weekend, a plan that never converges): metered spend keeps accruing and the only stops are the operator's; the board RETRY row, node.retry events, the re-plan notifications and the reported cost_usd are the mitigation. The owner accepted this explicitly (R1-R3).

In the same TUI session `/kpi stop` cannot reach a running loop because the command handler holds the input queue (interactive-mode.ts L1188-1191, L3176-3179; agent-session.ts L1357): the in-flight stops are Ctrl+C (process exit, resumable because every wait is preceded by a checkpoint), a gate choice, or `/kpi stop` from a second session. The stop marker lands only at the next superstep or after the current backoff (up to 60 s) and a node mid-prompt finishes its prompt first. rejected: critique-1's alternative of detaching the loop from the command handler — the loop drives ctx.ui gates (confirm/select/editor) from inside the handler and the parent session would start accepting prompts mid-loop; that is a larger, riskier change than a durable marker, and it is recorded here as an open question for the owner.

This narrows R4's 'must count as live/resumable' to 'resumable'; the eight legacy UNSAFE/EXHAUSTED runs on disk stay finished and resume only when named. If the owner wants paused jobs live, AC-24.3 must be amended in the same change (contract conflict per AGENTS.md rule 7).

Witnesses stay on review verdicts only (gated-loop.ts L1493-1512), so an implement↔test inner loop that never reaches review has no progress detection now that maxNodeRuns is gone; it is visible on the board (NODE alternating, evidence lamp) but silent in events. rejected: critique-2's optional evidence-fingerprint inner-loop witness is not added — it would either change ROUND semantics or need a second witness set; listed as an open question.

Edge exclusivity: route() (engine.ts L798-820) unions every firing edge, so the four REVISE edges must be exactly exclusive over progress.repeated × plan.repair_tried × plan.provided or a superstep schedules implement and plan together. The graph-routing test enumerates all eight combinations.

Resuming a no_progress pause (Keep going / Give guidance / unattended /kpi <job>) re-runs the plan node even for a --plan job: the automatic path never re-plans a provided plan, but the operator-initiated resume revises it (gated mode gates the revision at plan-approval; autopilot does not). rejected: critique-1's suggestion to route a --plan job's repeat to plan-check/pass-through — that would leave the operator no way to give guidance, and the re-plan there is the operator's own choice.

progress.repeated is computed from verdict.json on every superstep, so after the driver records a verdict the next supersteps also see repeated=true; only edges from review read it, and a future graph reading it elsewhere would see a stale witness. Documented in spec §7.

A re-plan clears task.current_module_id and rewrites stack.json; freezeCurrentSlice (stack.ts L504-518) re-freezes from the new stack. A plan whose stack fails validation after a re-plan pauses NEEDS_HUMAN/stack — the operator sees a stack pause, not a no-progress one.

The fixture-based resume test depends on research.json task_hash and stack.json freshness matching the copied task.json (research/gate.ts L244-250, stack.ts L495-518); the fixture is committed under test/fixtures/retired-cap-resume so those hashes are frozen together, and mtimes are restored by writing task.json before stack.json.

Backoff ceiling 60 s without jitter means concurrent nodes (maxConcurrency 2) retry in lockstep against a rate-limited provider; the accounts balancer's cooling/failover (accounts/index.ts L691-720) spreads load, not the engine.
httpIdleTimeoutMs: 0 disables the per-request timeout (sdk.ts L346-348), and a hung provider is then never retried; spec §6 names this.
